definition: Moral rhetoric is language that explicitly invokes ethical values, duties, rights, dignity, fairness, equality, compassion, civic virtue, or moral condemnation in order to evaluate people, institutions, policies, or social conditions.
clarification: Code as moral rhetoric when the text does more than state a policy or practical consequence and instead frames an issue in terms of what is right, fair, deserved, respectful, humane, inclusive, or obligatory. This includes references to rights, equality, discrimination, protection of vulnerable people, unjust treatment, freedom as a normative value, compassion for suffering, and praise or condemnation using moral virtues or vices.

positive_examples.text: Every person, however frail or vulnerable, has a place and a purpose in this world.
positive_examples.explanation: The assertion that every person, including those who are frail or vulnerable, has a place and purpose affirms intrinsic human worth.

positive_examples.text: We will establish a comprehensive race equality strategy to break down the barriers still faced by black and minority ethnic communities.
positive_examples.explanation: The commitment to race equality and breaking down barriers directly invokes equality and inclusion as moral values.

positive_examples.text: While no one should be denied access to the courts, the rule of lawyers threatens our global competitiveness, denies Americans access to the quality of justice they deserve, and puts every small business one lawsuit away from bankruptcy.
positive_examples.explanation: The statement explicitly says no one should be denied access to courts and invokes justice people deserve.

negative_clarification: Do not code texts that merely announce programmes, funding, regulations, administrative reforms, economic outcomes, factual trends, or technical policy mechanisms. Terms such as efficient, accessible, transparent, sustainable, adequate, or priority are not sufficient on their own unless they are tied to an explicit ethical claim such as fairness, rights, dignity, discrimination, or protection from injustice.

negative_examples.text: We will continue to develop Plaid Cymru’s Inspire Wales programme to involve all ages in sporting activity and ensure our people stay fit and healthy.
negative_examples.explanation: This promotes sports participation and health but contains no explicit ethical value judgment, right, or fairness claim.

negative_examples.text: Simplifying Tax Compliance: We will allow all companies to base their preliminary corporation tax returns on prior year tax liabilities, reducing their need to hire advisers to estimate their current year tax liabilities before the year is finished.
negative_examples.explanation: This is a technical proposal to simplify corporate tax compliance, framed entirely in administrative and economic terms.

negative_examples.text: Development of a land transition plan which will include regulation of farming practices to reduce environmental damage,
negative_examples.explanation: This proposes farming regulation to reduce environmental damage but does not explicitly frame the proposal in moral terms.
